messages.author: ea99f640d3869c3c
messages.subject: facet_window or facet_page
parts:
I was wondering if there was a way in ggpot2 to create a new faceting
option per page or window.
I often have data sets with 100 or more groups. If I use facet_wrap or
facet_grid I get the plot I am looking for but the facets are too
small to be of any use. I often have to resort to subsetting the data
to maybe 25 groups before plotting in ggplot2 and then plotting the
data 4 times to get all 100 groups down in graphs.

If there were a way in ggplot2 to be able to add an option in faceting
to wrap 25 groups per graph and then output 4 separate graphs, that
would save many steps. But I understand if this sort of thing is
beyond the capabilities of ggplot2. I was just thinking that maybe it
would be a nice feature to add to a future release of ggplot2 or if
somebody new of a method to do something similar by placing ggplot
with a plyr function.

Dan Gillie

messages.author: 68b661fcb57b94a9
messages.subject: Re: facet_window or facet_page
parts:
You can create lists of individual plots and then plot them as you wish, like the following. But it doesn't make use of the faceting - so you'd have to manually (by way of a function) facet outside of ggplot2.

plt = list of ggplot objects
nrow, ncol = number of plots per page

function(plt, nrow, ncol)
{
loops <- ceiling(length(plt) / (nrow * ncol))
p <- 1
for (l in 1:loops) {
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(nrow, ncol)))
for (r in 1:nrow) for (c in 1:ncol) {
if (p > length(plt)) break
print(plt[[p]], vp=viewport(layout.pos.row=r, layout.pos.col=c))
p <- p + 1
}
}}



Adam Loveland
